Built for humans, wired for agents.
Loupe is free and open source under AGPL-3.0-or-later. Self-host it and it costs nothing, forever. Your documents, your comments and your database stay yours — there is no lock-in to walk away from.
Which agents does it work with?
Any agent that speaks Model Context Protocol. It authenticates with a scoped API token and calls
, and gets a shareable review URL back.
Can my agent track work in Loupe?

Yes. Your agent files cards on the project board over MCP, in the columns you set for each board, and links the pull requests that carry each one. An epic card groups the small cards of one large feature, and the board shows each epic as a swimlane with its progress. Each board follows a workflow template, so Loupe moves a card through its stages and asks your bridge for the next piece of work. When you connect a repository through the GitHub App, Loupe follows the pull request of each card, shows its checks, conflicts and review on the board, and can carry it through to the merge.
Do reviewers need to be technical?
No. They open a URL and read rendered Markdown. Selecting text and leaving a comment is the whole interaction. No repository access, no terminal, no diff to parse.
What happens to a comment when the document changes?
Anchors are re-located against the new text. When the quoted passage is genuinely gone, the thread stays and says so rather than silently attaching itself to the wrong paragraph.
Can I move from hosted to self-hosted later?
Yes, it is the same application. Export your data and run the container. The AGPL licence guarantees you the source either way.

Comment on the pull request when a fix run is queued

Loupe posts a new comment on the GitHub pull request each time a bridge queues a fix run for it. The GitHub App needs "Pull requests: read and write". It needs a bridge that reports the event that queued a run. An older bridge sends none, so no comment posts.
Comment on a pull request when new commits follow its approval
An approval that does not cover the newest commit starts no merge. Loupe then posts one comment on the GitHub pull request for that commit. The GitHub App needs "Pull requests: read and write".
Not merged: commit `%sha%` came after your approval. Approve the new head to merge.
Sync an approved pull request that is behind
Loupe updates the branch of the next approved pull request that is behind its base, one at a time. The GitHub App needs "Contents: read and write".
Merge a pull request when the workflow asks
Loupe merges a pull request when the workflow of the board asks for it. The GitHub App needs "Contents: read and write".
Change the base of a pull request when the workflow asks
Loupe changes the base branch of a pull request when the workflow of the board asks for it. The GitHub App needs "Pull requests: read and write".
Switch an epic pull request between draft and ready when the workflow asks
Loupe marks the pull request of an epic as a draft while the epic is in implementation, and as ready when it moves to review. The GitHub App needs "Pull requests: read and write".
Close the pull requests of an epic when the workflow asks
Loupe closes the pull requests of an epic that a person moves back to the Backlog. The GitHub App needs "Pull requests: read and write".
